scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7103: HELP!!! Our whole site is CUT OFF from everything!!
None of us here can reach anything at all -- not the other sites, not even our
own gateway thing, NOTHING. Something around the first box out of the room
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone reconnect us, and HURRY,
the whole office is just sitting here!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. Location C's gateway (router4 LAN interface,
  192.168.200.1) is up; PC11-PC14 reach it with 0% loss; and Location C exchanges
  traffic with the rest of the network over the RIP core -- Location A reaches
  Location C (PC4 -> 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts) with 0% loss,
  so the inter-site path is forwarding in both directions. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a total Location C
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Location C totally cut off
from its gateway and the rest of the network -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches
its gateway 192.168.200.1 (router4 LAN) with 0% loss, and the inter-site path is
up (Location A's PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 Location C
hosts with 0% loss), so Location C is exchanging traffic across the RIP core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: Location C's gateway and its inter-site
connectivity are healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct
agent reproduces the claimed failures -- PC11 -> gateway and a cross-site path
(e.g. PC4 <-> Location C) -- finds them working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" an isolated Location C, a downed router4, or a severed RIP link to
satisfy the "totally cut off" ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: router6’s firewall (iptables) on the uplink interface. Hosts in the 172.18.51.0/24 site can reach their local gateway but are isolated from all other networks due to forwarding policy on router6.

Mechanism: End hosts (e.g., pc15 172.18.51.15) can ping their default gateway 172.18.51.254 and other local hosts (172.18.51.16), proving local L2/L3 is fine. Router6 itself can ping remote subnets (e.g., router6 → 172.16.10.4 succeeds), so routing is up. However, client-to-remote pings (pc15/pc16 → 172.16.10.4 or 192.168.200.14) time out. On router6, iptables FORWARD chain contains blanket drops for any packets arriving on eth2 (the upstream/WAN interface): “-A FORWARD -i eth2 -j DROP” (plus TCP/UDP-specific drops). This drops all return traffic from the WAN to the LAN, breaking all off-subnet communications from the site and preventing inbound reachability to 172.18.51.0/24.

Localization: router6, interface eth2 (10.50.1.2), iptables FORWARD chain. Routing table shows RIP-learned routes are present; the failure is purely filtering.

Root cause: A misconfigured iptables rule set on router6 is dropping all forwarded packets arriving on eth2, inadvertently cutting the site off from the rest of the network.

Corrective fix: Remove/adjust the eth2 drop rules and permit established/related return traffic. For example:
- iptables -D FORWARD -i eth2 -j DROP (remove the blanket drops)
- iptables -A FORWARD -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
- Ensure appropriate LAN→WAN allow rules exist, then save/persist the corrected rules.

per_axis.rationale: The agent's writeup does not mention the baseline observations that PC11–PC14 reach gateway 192.168.200.1 or that Location A reaches Location C across the RIP core with 0% loss.

The agent's conclusion that router6's FORWARD rules are dropping forwarded traffic is well supported by observed local pings succeeding, router6 being able to reach remotes, and an iptables FORWARD chain that drops packets arriving on eth2. A minor ungrounded detail is mapping eth2 to the upstream/WAN interface and one stated IP for eth2, which wasn't shown in the log.
